instruction: Save a snapshot of this video frame as 'trailer_frame.png' in the Documents folder.

parameters.window_name: Interstellar Movie - Interstellar Movie - Official Trailer - VLC media player

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully took a VLC snapshot via Video > Take Snapshot menu, then used terminal to move and rename the file from ~/Pictures/vlcsnap-*.png to ~/Desktop/interstellar.png.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate VLC menus, use Take Snapshot, open terminal, use mv/ls commands for file management
metadata.task_rationale: Same snapshot task with different target filename and directory (Documents instead of Desktop) to test generalization of file placement skills
metadata.explanation: Task requires taking a VLC snapshot and saving it to ~/Documents/ with a specific name. Getter checks file existence, MIME type, and size via bash. Partial credit: 0.5 for file existence, 0.3 for valid image type, 0.2 for reasonable size.

scoring_breakdown.file_exists: 0.5 - Snapshot file exists at target path
scoring_breakdown.valid_image: 0.3 - File is a valid image (image/* MIME type)

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly checks file existence at the exact path specified in the instruction (/home/user/Documents/trailer_frame.png) using bash commands (test -f, file --mime-type, stat)
Metric provides reasonable partial credit scoring: 0.5 for file existence, 0.3 for valid image MIME type, 0.2 for reasonable file size (>1KB)
All instruction requirements are covered: correct filename (trailer_frame.png), correct location (Documents folder), and valid image content
No postconfig needed since file system state persists after the agent's actions
Minor note: metric receives expected parameter with expected_path but never uses it - path enforcement happens via getter config instead, which is functionally correct but redundant
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider having the metric validate that result['path'] matches expected['expected_path'] for additional robustness, though this is not strictly necessary since the getter is already configured with the correct path
